simple: The MicroProfiler can record the data your game sends and receives over the internet. This helps you find out why a game feels laggy or takes a long time to load. You turn on network capture, save a frame dump, and open it in a web browser. The charts show downloads and uploads per frame, colored by type, and you can click to see each network event.
analogy: It is like tracking every package that comes to and leaves your house. You can see which day had the most deliveries and open each box to see what was inside.
keyPoints: Network data only appears in saved frame dumps from the desktop client or Studio, not in the live overlay.
Open the MicroProfiler (Ctrl+Alt+F6) and pick High, Low, or Off in the Network menu.
High records more detail, like each item in a batch and asset IDs. Low is the default and is lighter, so dumps can hold more frames.
Save the frame data, open the HTML file, then pick X-Ray / Network to see the charts.
The top row is received traffic (downloads) and the bottom row is sent traffic (uploads).
Bars are colored by type: blue for physics, green for data, red for assets.
If a few big spikes hide everything else, turn on Options / Log Scale Graph.
Right-click a bar to open the Network events window with details for each event.

terms.network traffic: All the data going between a player's device and the server.
terms.frame dump: A saved recording of many frames of profiler data that you open in a web browser.
terms.packet: A small chunk of data sent over the network.
terms.batch: Many small items bundled into one packet to send them together.
terms.deserialize: Turn received data back into game things, like turning a packet into a property change.
terms.verbosity: How much detail is recorded. High verbosity records more but is more work for your computer.
terms.log scale: A graph scale where each step is 10 times bigger. A bar for 10 KB and one for 1,000 KB both stay visible, instead of the small one shrinking to almost nothing.
terms.Rx and Tx: Short for receive and transmit. Rx is data coming in, Tx is data going out.
terms.latency: Delay between something happening and others seeing it.

watchOut: Looking for network data in the live overlay. It only shows in saved dumps.
